To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• The fully self-consistent WARP-POSIST code suite has been extended to simulate the interaction between electron clouds and ultrarelativisitic beams.
(i) The fully self-consistent method is practical for the modeling of beams with ultrarelativisitic velocities.

(i) the use of a preferred frame of references reduces the cost of fully-self-consistent simulations of the interaction of ultrarrelativistic beams with electron clouds by several orders of magnitude; (ii) the computational cost of the quasi-static and fully self-consistent approaches are comparable when using a number of stations per bunch period that is larger than one, which is the case for most high intensity beams in accelerators.« less
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a new approach to modeling the interaction between electron clouds and beams in high energy accelerations, based on the use of a fully self-consistentsimulation of both electron clouds and beams, in which the evolution of both the beam and electron cloud distributions are followed simultaneously, without any restriction on the relative motion of the two.
the development of numerical methods and their implementation in WARP-POSIST to enable the fully self-consist simulation of the interaction between beams and electron clouds.
the study of the interaction of electron clouds with beams in accelerators.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the case of a single bunch interacting with an electron cloud, the fully self-consistency approach is not yet practical, and a quasi-static approach is needed.

, for the quasi-static approach, the minimum number of stations per beam period should be 1, and that, for the fully self-consist approach, the minimum is 1/4, and that, in both cases, the number of stations should be increased until the emittance growth saturates.

the fully self-consistently simulated electron cloud effects are not a concern for the operation of the HIE-ISOLDE linac, and that the electron cloud effects can be safely studied with a reduced model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fully self-consist approach, as it stands, cannot be used to simulate the electron cloud effects in the presence of strong magnetic fields.
the fully self-consistant approach is practical and that the cost is comparable to that of a single bunch simulation.
the fully self-consitent simulation with WARP-Posinst has been successfully applied for the simulation of the beam-electron cloud interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for electron clouds with a typical density of a few electrons per bunch, the fully self-consistently simulated electron cloud is not significantly different from a prescribed cloud.
, for the case of the LHC, it is not practical.

, while fully self-consistent PIC simulations are feasible, they are still very expensive and are not yet a viable option for the simulation of electron cloud buildup and beam dynamics in high energy accelerations.
